doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

title: Buying jazz LPs from a multipurpose store
summary: With no record store in the village, she bought every saxophone LP being sold off in a school-town store.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: How did you pursue hearing more jazz? Was there record stores in your town? Were there radio stations that you could find that would play it?

Well it’s funny that you mention that but you know coming from such a small village there was no record store or anything but in the town where my high school was there was a sort of a, you know you could buy anything from eyeglasses to cameras to — it was sort of a multipurpose store and they also had a little music department. And I guess © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

there was not much interest in jazz LPs at the time of course, so they wanted to get things sold for like a dollar for an LP, they sold off all the jazz LPs. And I just happened to walk into that store at that time. And I bought everything that had a saxophone on it. And I didn’t know, you know I had everything from of course Charlie Parker, Phil Woods, Ornette Coleman, then Grover Washington Jr., Coltrane, but just the most — I listened to — and David Sanborn it was like how can David Sanborn and Phil Woods and Cannonball Adderley and Ornette Coleman, how can these all be jazz? I couldn’t reconcile this diversity at first, I thought wow, what is all of this and so slowly — I heard Ornette Coleman playing the violin I thought my God what is he doing, I had no idea you know.
